On the eve of Apple's special event, Bloomberg published a new report detailing the decade-long development process of the foldable iPhone.

The report specifically mentions former Apple CEO Tim Cook's involvement in the project, as well as the possible price of the foldable iPhone.

Mark Gurman pointed out that Apple engineers began development work on the iPhone Fold around 2016. In 2020, after returning from a business trip to China, Cook was 'unusually excited' about foldable phones. He reportedly pushed Apple's hardware team to accelerate the development of the company's first foldable product.

Cook has traditionally 'not been involved in the conception of new products', so his participation in the development of the foldable iPhone gives the project even more weight:

As for the pricing of the foldable iPhone (internally referred to by everyone at Apple as the iPhone Ultra), the company's original target was an entry-level price of US$1,999. However, this target has recently been raised to US$2,199 due to rising component costs.

According to one person familiar with the matter, Apple recently discussed pricing the foldable product as high as US$2,199, and said multiple options have been considered in recent weeks, with the memory shortage causing Apple's cost targets to be significantly exceeded. Some versions with larger storage capacities could approach US$3,000. By comparison, the standard iPhone currently starts at US$799, while the iPhone 17 Pro starts at US$1,099.

Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone Ultra tomorrow. 9to5Mac will be on-site at the Steve Jobs Theater to provide in-depth coverage of all the details.
